examples.ko: 청소할 때는 쓸고 나서 걸레질까지 해야 해요.
examples.en: When cleaning, you need to sweep and then mop too.
I mopped hard, and the floor became clean.
After mopping, I break a sweat.
I'll take care of the mopping today.
Mopping is hard on my back, so it's tiring.
The kids helped with the mopping too.

explain: 걸레로 바닥이나 가구를 닦는 일이에요. 청소기를 돌리는 일과 구별해서 말하고, 물에 적신 걸레로 닦으면 '물걸레질'이라고도 해요. '걸레질을 하다'나 '걸레질하다' 둘 다 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I mop the room every Sunday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걸레질을 하다'와 같은 뜻으로 한 낱말처럼 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 걸레질을 하다, said as one short word.

phrases.en: After vacuuming, I also wet-mop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 적신 걸레로 닦는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wiping with a wet cloth.

phrases.en: I finished mopping and opened the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소 순서를 말할 때 '끝내다'와 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with 끝내다 when describing cleaning steps.

explain_en: It is the work of wiping floors or furniture with a rag. It is distinguished from vacuuming, and wiping with a wet rag can be called '물걸레질'. Both '걸레질을 하다' and '걸레질하다' sound natural.

examples.en: A man was shouting at the top of his lungs on the street.

examples.ko: 동네가 떠나가게 고래고래 외치는 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: Someone was yelling so loudly that the whole neighborhood could hear.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 고래고래 울었어요.
examples.en: The child bawled loudly, asking me to buy a toy.

examples.ko: 옆집에서 밤새 고래고래 싸우는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: All night I heard loud shouting from the next door.

examples.ko: 고래고래 소리 지르지 말고 조용히 말해요.
examples.en: Don't yell at the top of your voice; speak quietly.

examples.ko: 축구 경기를 보며 친구가 고래고래 응원했어요.
examples.en: My friend cheered at the top of his voice while watching the soccer match.

explain: '소리를 지르다, 외치다, 울다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 화가 났거나 흥분해서 시끄럽게 내는 소리일 때가 많아서 대체로 부정적인 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: He got angry and shouted at the top of his voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 말을 아주 큰 소리로 외치는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of shouting what you want to say at a very loud volume.
phrases.en_equiv: to shout at the top of one's voice

phrases.example: 술에 취한 사람이 고래고래 노래를 불러요.
phrases.en: A drunk person is singing at the top of his lungs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시끄럽게 노래하는 모습을 말하고 보통 좋지 않은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes noisy singing, usually with a negative feel.

phrases.example: 옆집 사람이 밤늦게 고래고래 소리를 질러서 잠을 못 잤어요.
phrases.en: My neighbor was yelling loudly late at night, so I couldn't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나거나 흥분해서 시끄럽게 소리를 지를 때 써요. 대체로 부정적인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for yelling noisily out of anger or excitement; usually has a negative feel.

explain_en: It goes with verbs like '소리를 지르다', '외치다' and '울다'. It usually describes noisy shouting out of anger or excitement, so it tends to sound negative.

examples.ko: 친구들이 저를 골탕 먹이려고 거짓말을 했어요.
examples.en: My friends lied to me to play a prank on me.

examples.ko: 장난으로 동생을 골탕 먹였다가 엄마한테 혼났어요.
examples.en: I played a prank on my younger sibling and got scolded by Mom.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 알려 줘서 큰 골탕을 먹었어요.
examples.en: They gave me the wrong directions and I got into real trouble.
Check ahead of time so you don't get stuck.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서 바가지를 써서 골탕만 먹었어요.
examples.en: I got overcharged at that shop and just came away worse off.
Who's trying to mess with me?

explain: 거의 '먹다/먹이다'와 한 덩어리로 써요. '골탕을 먹다'는 당하는 쪽, '골탕을 먹이다'는 하는 쪽이에요. 큰 사고라기보다 속거나 곤란해지는 일에 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 동생이 저를 골탕 먹이려고 의자에 풀을 발랐어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling put glue on my chair to play a prank on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 속이거나 곤란하게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 장난으로도, 조금 심하게도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to deliberately fool someone or put them in a bind. It can be a playful prank or something a bit meaner.

explain_en: It is almost always used together with '먹다' or '먹이다'. '골탕을 먹다' is being on the receiving end, while '골탕을 먹이다' is doing it to someone. It suits being tricked or put in a tough spot rather than a serious accident.

en: to be replaced; to be substituted; to be changed

examples.en: The old computer was replaced with a new one.
Two players are substituted in the second half.

examples.ko: 고장 난 부품은 곧 교체될 거예요.
examples.en: The broken part will be replaced soon.

examples.ko: 감독이 교체된 뒤 팀 분위기가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After the coach was replaced, the team's mood changed.
The filter has to be replaced every month.
The old sign is being replaced.

explain: '바뀌다'보다 부품, 사람, 선수처럼 같은 자리에 있던 것을 다른 것으로 갈아 끼운다는 느낌이에요. 새것으로 바꾸는 상황에 쓰고, 단순히 달라지는 것에는 '바뀌다'를 써요. 능동은 '교체하다'로 '배터리를 교체하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I replace the battery with a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교체되다'의 능동형으로, 바꾸는 사람이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the person doing the replacing is the subject.

phrases.en: It's time to replace the filter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부품이나 소모품을 갈아야 할 때를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the time to change a part or consumable.

phrases.en: The coach substituted a player in the second half.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 경기에서 선수가 다른 선수로 바뀔 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard phrase for swapping a player in a sports match.

explain_en: Compared with 바뀌다, it means swapping what sat in a spot, like a part, person or player, for another. Use it for replacement with something new; for simply becoming different, use 바뀌다. The active 교체하다 appears in '배터리를 교체하다'.

examples.en: I was so sick that I couldn't move from my bed.
If you budge, they'll find us, so keep quiet.

examples.ko: 추워서 하루 종일 집에서 꼼짝하기 싫었어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I didn't want to budge from home all day.

examples.ko: 고양이가 무서운지 꼼짝하지 않고 숨어 있어요.
examples.en: The cat must be scared, because it's hiding without moving a muscle.

examples.ko: 꼼짝하는 사람이 없을 만큼 영화가 재미있었어요.
examples.en: The movie was so good that nobody stirred.

examples.ko: 차가 막혀서 한 시간 동안 꼼짝하지도 못했어요.
examples.en: The traffic was so bad that we couldn't move at all for an hour.

explain: 거의 항상 '꼼짝하지 못하다', '꼼짝하지 않다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써요. 영화나 만화에서 듣는 '꼼짝 마!'는 움직이지 말라는 명령이에요. '꼼짝없이'는 어쩔 수 없다는 느낌의 다른 부사예요.

phrases.example: 그는 아내 앞에서는 꼼짝 못 해요.
phrases.en: be completely under someone's thumb
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서워서나 약점이 있어서 상대가 하라는 대로 해야 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has to do whatever another person says because of fear or a weakness.

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '꼼짝하지 못하다' or '꼼짝하지 않다'. The '꼼짝 마!' you hear in movies and comics is an order meaning 'freeze!'. '꼼짝없이' is a different adverb that gives a feeling of having no way out.

examples.en: We're late, so don't dawdle, let's head out quickly.
A caterpillar is wriggling on the leaf.
Every morning I dawdle in bed and end up being late.
If you dawdle like that, you'll miss the train.
There's no time to dawdle, so hurry up.
The child dawdled for a long time while changing clothes.

explain: 벌레처럼 느리게 꿈틀대는 움직임에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 행동이 느려서 재촉할 때 '꾸물거리지 마'라고 많이 말해요. 약간 답답해하는 말투가 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해서 써요.

phrases.en: I dawdled and missed the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-다가'를 붙여 느리게 굴어서 생긴 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-다가' you can say what resulted from dawdling.

phrases.en: I dawdle every morning, so I'm often late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꾸물거리다'와 뜻이 거의 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as '꾸물거리다', so the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: A bug is crawling slowly on the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느리게 꿈틀거리는 움직임을 나타내는 부사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb for slow, wriggling movement.

explain_en: It can describe slow wriggling like a worm's, but in daily life it is mostly used to urge someone on, as in '꾸물거리지 마'. It carries a slightly impatient tone, so be careful using it toward elders.

en: to fall down; to tumble down; to be thrown down

examples.en: I slipped on the ice and fell flat on my back.
The child was startled and just fell over.
The chair broke and I tumbled over backward.
It's really embarrassing to fall flat on the street.
Be careful not to fall on the snowy road.

examples.ko: 동생은 공을 차다가 나자빠져서 웃음거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: My younger brother fell over while kicking the ball and became a laughingstock.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 벌렁 뒤로 쓰러지는 느낌이 강한 입말이에요. '일은 안 하고 나자빠져 있다'처럼 빈둥거리며 누워 있다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: I was so surprised that I almost fell flat on my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌렁 뒤로 쓰러지는 모습을 나타내는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for falling flat on your back.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall flat on one's back

phrases.en: I slipped on the road and fell flat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 크게 넘어졌다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form saying you fell down hard.

phrases.example: 주말에는 하루 종일 소파에 나자빠져 있어요.
phrases.en: On weekends I just lounge on the sofa all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일은 안 하고 누워 빈둥거린다는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also means lounging around lazily instead of working.

explain_en: Compared with '넘어지다', it suggests flopping over backward and is a spoken word. It can also mean lying around idly, as in '일은 안 하고 나자빠져 있다'.

en: to push; to thrust; to shove

examples.en: My friend shoved me as a joke.

examples.ko: 부모님의 재촉에 떠밀려 결혼 준비를 시작했어요.
examples.en: Pushed by my parents' urging, I started preparing for marriage.
I got pushed along by the crowd and ended up getting off the subway.
Don't push the work off onto your younger sibling.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 떠미는 바람에 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: Someone pushed me from behind and I almost fell.
They are passing the responsibility back and forth to each other.

explain: '밀다'보다 힘으로 거칠게 밀어내는 느낌이 있어요. 책임이나 일을 남에게 넘길 때도 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '떠넘기다'가 있어요. '떠밀려 ~하다'는 어쩔 수 없이 하게 됐다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Even if it's crowded, please don't push each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 거칠게 밀지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask someone not to shove people.

phrases.en: I was pushed by my friends into singing a song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶지 않았지만 주변 때문에 어쩔 수 없이 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you did something unwillingly because of others' pressure.

phrases.en: Don't pass your work off onto your younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떠밀다'와 비슷하게 일이나 책임을 남에게 넘길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 떠밀다 when handing off work or responsibility to someone else.

explain_en: It feels rougher and more forceful than plain '밀다'. It is also used when passing off responsibility or work to others, similar to '떠넘기다'. The pattern '떠밀려 ~하다' means being pushed into doing something against your will.

examples.en: I don't want to get dragged into my friends' fight.
My sleeve almost got caught in the machine.
I had a hard time after getting caught up in that incident.
I rescued a person being swept into the waves.
Be careful not to get mixed up in bad things.
The child struggled after being caught up in a rumor.

explain: '휘말리다'와 거의 같게 써요. 내가 원하지 않았는데 싸움, 사고, 소문 같은 나쁜 일에 끌려 들어갈 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I got caught up in a rumor and felt stressed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말려들다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 나쁜 일에 끌려 들어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 말려들다, used when being dragged into something bad.

phrases.en: I got drawn into a fight between strangers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말로, 원하지 않았는데 싸움에 끌려 들어간 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for being pulled into a fight you didn't want.
phrases.en_equiv: to get drawn into a fight

phrases.en: Don't get involved in those people's business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 나쁜 일에 끼지 말라고 조언할 때 쓰는 존댓말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way of advising someone not to get dragged into trouble.

explain_en: It is used almost like 휘말리다. It describes being pulled into trouble such as a fight, an accident or a rumor when you didn't want to be. It is not used for good things.

examples.en: I made a slip of the tongue in the interview and turned red.

examples.ko: 그는 예전에 했던 말실수가 생각나서 밤새 잠을 이루지 못했어요.
examples.en: He remembered a slip he once made and couldn't sleep all night.

examples.ko: 말실수 한 번 때문에 오해가 생겼어요.
examples.en: One verbal slip caused a misunderstanding.
Anyone can make a verbal slip.

examples.ko: 말실수로 친구 기분을 상하게 해서 사과했어요.
examples.en: I hurt my friend's feelings with a slip of the tongue and apologized.

examples.ko: 방송에서 말실수도 웃음으로 넘기는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people laugh off even their on-air slips of the tongue.

explain: 틀린 말을 하거나 해서는 안 될 말을 무심코 해 버린 것을 모두 가리켜요. '실언'도 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이고, 일상에서는 '말실수를 하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I was nervous and made a slip of the tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말실수'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase with 말실수.

phrases.en: Because of a slip of the tongue, things got awkward with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말실수가 어떤 일의 이유가 될 때 '때문에'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '때문에' to say a verbal slip caused something.
phrases.en_equiv: because of a slip of the tongue

phrases.en: You have to be careful not to make slips of the tongue in an interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말실수를 하지 않도록 주의하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you should take care not to say the wrong thing.

explain_en: It covers both saying a wrong word and carelessly saying something you shouldn't have. '실언' is similar but stiffer, while in daily speech '말실수를 하다' sounds natural.

examples.en: My shoe was swept away by the waves and disappeared.
I got pushed along by the crowd and ended up at the exit.

examples.ko: 지하철 문이 열리자 사람들 사이로 밀려갔어요.
examples.en: When the subway doors opened, I was pushed along among the people.
The boat is being pushed along by the wind.
The line is long, so I keep getting pushed back.
The sight of leaves drifting along on the ripples is pretty.

explain: '밀리다'(힘에 밀리다)에 '가다'가 붙어서, 내 뜻과 상관없이 어떤 방향으로 움직이는 모습이에요. 반대 방향은 '밀려오다'예요. 힘을 주어 미는 사람이 따로 있을 때는 '밀어 가다'가 아니라 '밀다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The balloon was pushed away by the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 물처럼 힘이 센 것에 움직여질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is moved by a strong force like wind or water.
phrases.en_equiv: to be pushed away by the wind

phrases.en: The trash is being carried away by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that the movement is happening right now.

phrases.en: I tied the boat with a rope so it wouldn't drift away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않게 움직이는 것을 막으려 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when trying to prevent unwanted movement.
phrases.en_equiv: so that it doesn't get pushed away

explain_en: It combines '밀리다' (be pushed) and '가다', showing something moving in a direction regardless of its own will. The opposite direction is '밀려오다'. When a person is deliberately pushing something, use '밀다' instead.

examples.en: My phone battery is completely dead.

examples.ko: 폰이 방전돼서 길을 찾을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: My phone ran out of charge, so I couldn't find the way.
The car's battery is dead and it won't start.
Plug in the charger before it runs out of power.

examples.ko: 오래 쓰지 않은 배터리는 저절로 방전돼요.
examples.en: A battery left unused for a long time drains by itself.
Where can I charge a drained power bank?

explain: 배터리나 전기 기구에서 전기가 다 떨어졌을 때 써요. 사람이 너무 지쳤을 때 '완전히 방전됐다'고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 반대말은 '충전되다'예요.

phrases.en: Charge it before it dies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배터리가 다 닳기 전에 하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to tell someone to act before the battery runs out.

phrases.example: 자동차 배터리가 방전돼서 시동이 안 걸려요.
phrases.en: The car battery is dead, so it won't start.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차 배터리에도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning applies to a car battery.

phrases.en: I worked all week, so I'm completely drained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 너무 지쳤을 때 농담처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used jokingly when a person is totally exhausted.

explain_en: It is used when a battery or electrical device has run out of electricity. People also joke '완전히 방전됐다' when they are completely worn out. The opposite is '충전되다' (get charged).

examples.en: The child broke a toy sword and cried.
I kept breaking the pencil lead, so I sharpened it again.

examples.ko: 젓가락을 두 손으로 잡고 부러뜨려 보세요.
examples.en: Hold the chopstick with both hands and try to snap it.
The typhoon snapped a big tree branch and passed.

examples.ko: 실수로 안경 다리를 부러뜨려서 안경점에 갔어요.
examples.en: I accidentally broke the arm of my glasses, so I went to the optician.

examples.ko: 마른 나뭇가지는 손으로도 쉽게 부러뜨릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Dry branches can be snapped easily even by hand.

explain: '부러지다'는 저절로 부러지는 것이고, '부러뜨리다'는 누가 힘을 주어 또는 실수로 부러지게 하는 것이에요. '부러트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 뼈를 다쳤을 때는 보통 '다리가 부러졌어요'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I broke the chopsticks by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 실수로 부러지게 했을 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for when you made something break by accident.

phrases.en: My younger sibling broke the branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부러뜨리다'와 뜻이 같은 다른 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A variant form with the same meaning as 부러뜨리다.

phrases.en: The branch broke in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 한 일이 아니라 저절로 부러질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something breaks by itself, not caused by a person.

explain_en: '부러지다' is when something snaps on its own, while '부러뜨리다' is when someone makes it snap, on purpose or by accident. '부러트리다' is an equivalent form. For an injured bone you usually say '다리가 부러졌어요'.

en: cutting in line; line jumping; line jumper

examples.ko: 줄을 서지 않고 새치기하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut in line without waiting your turn.
The person ahead cut in line, so I got angry.
I feel bad when I see someone cutting in line.
Even if you're in a hurry, please don't cut in line.

examples.ko: 버스를 탈 때 새치기한 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was someone who cut in line when boarding the bus.
Line-cutting was so bad that a staff member made an announcement.

explain: '새치기하다'로도, '새치기를 하다'로도 써요. 줄을 선 곳에서 차례를 어기고 끼어드는 것을 말하고, 운전할 때는 보통 '끼어들기'라고 해요. '새치'(흰머리)와 소리가 비슷하지만 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Someone cut in front of me in the bus line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 끼어들어서 내가 피해를 봤다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone cut in and you were affected.
phrases.en_equiv: to have someone cut in line

phrases.en: The entrance has a sign saying 'No cutting in line.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 자주 보는 짧은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase often seen on signs.

phrases.en: A car suddenly cut in front of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전할 때나 줄에서 사이에 들어올 때 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for cutting in while driving or in line.

explain_en: It can be used as '새치기하다' or '새치기를 하다'. It refers to breaking the order where people are lined up, and while driving people usually say '끼어들기'. It sounds like '새치' (gray hair) but is a different word.

en: to do an errand; to go on an errand

examples.en: My mom was sick, so I ran the errand for her.
The child went to the shop to run an errand.

examples.ko: 동생은 심부름하고 받은 용돈으로 과자를 샀어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling bought snacks with the allowance earned from running an errand.

examples.ko: 회사에서 신입이 심부름해야 하는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: At work, a new hire has many errands to run.
I will run the errands today, so please rest.
I gave a snack to the child who was running the errand.

explain: 대부분 '심부름을 가다', '심부름을 시키다'처럼 말해요. 심부름을 하는 사람은 '심부름꾼'이에요. 아이 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 어른끼리는 '부탁'이나 '잡일'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child went to the store on an errand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디로 가서 일을 해 주는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone goes somewhere to do a task for another.

phrases.en: My mom had me run an errand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 심부름을 하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have someone else run an errand.
phrases.en_equiv: to send someone on an errand

phrases.en: He is the errand runner of our shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심부름을 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for the person who runs errands.

explain_en: Usually it appears as '심부름을 가다' or '심부름을 시키다'. A person who does errands is a '심부름꾼'. It comes up a lot in stories about children; adults say '부탁' or '잡일' instead.

en: to be deferred; to be postponed

examples.en: The game is postponed because of rain.
The meeting was postponed to next week.
I do not know why the departure was delayed.
The event might be postponed.
The exam keeps being postponed.
The show was postponed, so I changed my ticket.

explain: 사람이 미루면 '연기하다', 일정이 미뤄지면 '연기되다'를 써요. 공지나 뉴스에서 '연기됐습니다'라는 말을 자주 들어요. 연기(演技, 연기하다)와 소리가 같으니 문장으로 구별해요.

phrases.en: Because of the rain, the departure was put off by a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연기되다'와 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 연기되다, but more casual and common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The travel schedule was postponed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일정'과 함께 쓰는 아주 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common collocation with 일정 (schedule).

phrases.en: Tomorrow's exam will not be postponed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미뤄지지 않고 그대로 한다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it will go ahead as planned.

explain_en: The active verb is for a person putting something off, and this passive is for a schedule that gets pushed back. It is common in announcements. It sounds the same as a word for acting, so context tells them apart.

examples.en: I dithered and missed the last bus.
He hesitated and couldn't answer.

examples.ko: 할 말이 있으면 우물쭈물하지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: If you have something to say, don't hesitate, just say it.
I hesitated in the interview, and I felt really sorry about it.

examples.ko: 아이가 문 앞에서 우물쭈물 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was standing at the door, hesitating.
While I was hesitating, the seats ran out.

explain: 자신이 없어서 말이나 행동을 확실히 못 하고 머뭇거릴 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '머뭇거리다', '주저하다'가 있는데, 우물쭈물은 조금 답답하고 소심해 보이는 느낌이에요. '우물쭈물하다'로도 많이 쓰고, 부정적인 말투일 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: Why are you hesitating so much?
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여 동사로 쓰는 가장 기본적인 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic verb form, adding '-하다'.

phrases.en: The chance is here, so don't hesitate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 망설이지 말라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to urge someone not to hesitate.

phrases.en: He hesitated in front of the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 '우물쭈물'보다 덜 답답한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but feels less frustrating than '우물쭈물'.

explain_en: It is used when someone hesitates in speech or action because they lack confidence. Similar words are '머뭇거리다' and '주저하다', but '우물쭈물' feels a bit frustrating and timid. It is also often used as '우물쭈물하다', and usually has a negative tone.

examples.en: The game was stopped because of the rain.
The construction suddenly stops.
What do I do if the internet service is cut off?
I don't know why the class was stopped.
The power went out and the work ended up halted.
Service will be suspended starting tomorrow.

explain: '중단되다'는 하던 일이 어떤 이유로 멈출 때 써요. 내가 일부러 멈추면 '중단하다', 저절로 멈추면 '중단되다'예요. 공사, 경기, 서비스, 운행 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: Service was temporarily suspended because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 멈췄다가 다시 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something stops briefly and will resume.

phrases.example: 중단된 공사가 다음 주에 다시 시작돼요.
phrases.en: The halted construction will start again next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중단된'으로 명사를 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form that describes a noun.

phrases.en: The service will not be interrupted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈추지 않고 계속된다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something continues without stopping.

explain_en: 중단되다 is used when something in progress stops because of some cause. If you stop it on purpose it is 중단하다, and if it stops by itself it is 중단되다. It often goes with words like construction, game, service and operation.

examples.en: There was a fire, so everyone escaped from the building.
The hero in the movie escapes from prison.
To escape, you have to go out through this door.
No one has escaped from there.
Let's look for a way to escape together.
I tried a game where you escape from a room.

explain: 갇힌 곳이나 위험한 곳에서 빠져나올 때 써요. '도망치다'는 쫓기는 느낌이 있고, '탈출하다'는 어렵게 벗어나는 느낌이 있어요. 조사는 '~에서 탈출하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I was happy because the main character succeeded in escaping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '탈출'을 써서 벗어나는 데 성공했다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '탈출' to say someone managed to get out.

phrases.en: The thief ran away when he saw the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쫓기는 느낌이 있고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels like being chased and is more common in daily speech.

phrases.example: 저는 이 복잡한 도시에서 탈출하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to escape from this busy city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 곳에서 벗어나고 싶은 마음을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used to say you want to get away from a hard place.

explain_en: Use it for getting out of a trapped or dangerous place. '도망치다' feels like running from a chaser, while '탈출하다' feels like breaking free with difficulty. The pattern is '~에서 탈출하다'.

dis.h: break out of confinement or danger

p.n: 탈출하다 stresses breaking free; 빠져나가다 stresses slipping out.

examples.en: The volcano suddenly erupts.
Gas exploded at the factory.
The anger I held back finally burst out.
Everyone evacuated before the bomb exploded.
Its popularity is exploding right now.
Be careful, because it could explode.

explain: 물건이 터질 때뿐 아니라 감정이 한꺼번에 터질 때도 써요. 인기나 관심이 갑자기 커질 때 '폭발적이다'라고도 해요. 작은 풍선은 '터지다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The anger I held back burst out all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 한꺼번에 터질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for emotions bursting out at once.

phrases.en: That song became explosively popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기가 갑자기 아주 커질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when popularity suddenly grows very large.

phrases.en: The balloon suddenly popped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 풍선이나 물건에는 '폭발하다'보다 '터지다'를 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For small things like balloons, '터지다' is more common.

explain_en: It describes things blowing up, and also emotions bursting out all at once. When popularity or interest suddenly grows, people say '폭발적이다'. For a small balloon, '터지다' is more common.

en: to escape; to flee; to take refugee

examples.en: When a shower came, I took shelter under the eaves.
If there's a fire, escape by the stairs.
We were sheltering in a mountain hut to avoid the blizzard.

examples.ko: 무서운 개를 보고 편의점으로 피신할까 했어요.
examples.en: I saw a scary dog and thought about ducking into a convenience store.

examples.ko: 폭우 때문에 높은 곳으로 피신하는 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people moved to high ground because of the heavy rain.

examples.ko: 잠시 어디론가 피신하고 싶을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I want to escape somewhere for a while.

explain: 피신하다는 '대피하다'와 비슷하지만, 사람이 스스로 몸을 숨기러 가는 느낌이 있어요. '도망치다'가 쫓기는 것에서 벗어나는 것이라면 피신하다는 안전한 곳이 목적지예요. '~로 피신하다'처럼 장소 뒤에 '로'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: If an earthquake happens, take shelter in a safe place.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'로 목적지를 붙여 어디로 피하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-(으)로' to name the destination you flee to.
phrases.en_equiv: to take shelter in a safe place

phrases.en: People hurried out of the building to safety.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급히'를 붙이면 서둘러 몸을 피하는 느낌이 더 커져요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Hurriedly' adds a sense of urgency to the escape.

phrases.en: When the announcement played, residents evacuated to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 안내나 뉴스에서 더 자주 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word more common in official notices and news.

explain_en: 피신하다 is close to 대피하다, but it has the feel of a person going off to hide on their own. While 도망치다 is breaking away from being chased, 피신하다 has a safe place as its destination. Attach 로 to the place, as in ~로 피신하다.

p.n: 피신하다 implies seeking safety; 도피하다 implies evading or running from something.

examples.en: There was a little incident on the subway yesterday.
That was a funny incident we could laugh off.

examples.ko: 해프닝 하나 때문에 회의가 잠깐 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The meeting stopped for a moment because of one little mishap.

examples.ko: 이름이 바뀐 해프닝은 지금 생각해도 웃겨요.
examples.en: The mix-up where the names got swapped is funny even now.
I'm glad it ended as just a small incident.

examples.ko: 여행 중 겪은 해프닝을 친구들에게 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I told my friends about the funny incident I had on the trip.

explain: 큰 사고가 아니라 웃고 넘길 수 있는 작은 일에 써요. '해프닝으로 끝나다', '해프닝이 벌어지다'처럼 말해요. 진지한 사건이나 다친 사람이 있는 일에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 일은 웃음만 남기고 해프닝으로 끝났어요.
phrases.en: That event ended as just a funny incident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 커지지 않고 가볍게 마무리됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something ends lightly without turning into a real problem.
phrases.en_equiv: to end as a funny incident

phrases.en: A small funny incident happened at the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃긴 일이 갑자기 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an amusing little thing suddenly happens.

phrases.en: What happened yesterday was a small incident.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작은'을 붙여 가벼운 일이라는 것을 더 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'small' makes it clearer that it was a minor, light matter.

explain_en: It is for small things you can laugh off, not for big accidents. People say '해프닝으로 끝나다' or '해프닝이 벌어지다'. It is not used for serious events or anything where someone was hurt.

examples.ko: 가게에 갔는데 문을 닫아서 허탕을 쳤어요.
examples.en: I went to the shop but it was closed, so it was a wasted trip.
I waited all day, and it came to nothing again today.
I went fishing but came back empty-handed.

examples.ko: 괜히 갔다가 허탕 칠까 봐 먼저 전화해 봤어요.
examples.en: I called first so I wouldn't make a wasted trip.
It ended up for nothing, and I felt so empty.

examples.ko: 두 시간을 헤맸는데 결국 허탕이 됐어요.
examples.en: I wandered for two hours and it all came to nothing.

explain: '허탕을 치다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요. 찾아가거나 기대했는데 헛걸음만 한 상황에 쓰고, 노력이 아무 결과 없이 끝났을 때도 말해요. 가볍게 투덜거릴 때 '아, 허탕이네' 하고 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to the hospital but it was closed, so it was a wasted trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가 봤지만 아무 소용없었을 때 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for going somewhere in vain.

phrases.example: 또 허탕 칠까 봐 먼저 전화해 봤어요.
phrases.en: I called first in case I came away empty-handed again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ까 봐'와 함께 걱정되는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -ㄹ까 봐, it expresses worry about wasting the trip.
phrases.en_equiv: for fear of coming away empty-handed

phrases.en: Ugh, that was a total waste.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대했는데 아무것도 못 했을 때 가볍게 투덜거리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light complaint when you got nothing out of your effort.

explain_en: The most common pairing is '허탕을 치다'. It is used when you went somewhere or expected something and made a wasted trip, and also when effort ended with no result. When grumbling lightly, people say '아, 허탕이네'.
